newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME nickel rises further in Asia, others easier.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel rises further in Asia, others easier.

text.p: London Metal Exchange nickel prices extended their sharp overnight gains during Asian trading hours on Thursday, although copper and aluminium edged lower from Wednesday evening's levels.
The nickel market, after a brief correction of its recent run-up, resumed its rally overnight.
Traders said news that workers at Russia's Norilsk, a major producer of nickel and platinum group metals, may strike from March 15 spurred speculative buying of those metals, traders said.
One trader expected further gains for nickel at Thursday's LME opening, with copper and aluminium also looking set to challenge the upside.
Copper and aluminium followed nickel higher in Wednesday evening trade but pulled back slightly during Asian hours.
At 0740 GMT, LME benchmark three-month nickel was quoted at $8,130/50 a tonne, up from $8,120 at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and $8,050 at the close of Wednesday's afternoon kerb.
Three-month copper was quoted at $2,410/15 a tonne versus $2,415 at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and $2,392 at the end of the afternoon kerb.
Aluminium was quoted at $1,668/71 a tonne, easing slightly from $1,671 at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and $1,665 at the afternoon kerb close.
